- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is negative or volatile (especially after recent spikes).
- Underestimate downward corrections after strong upward moves; model tends to overreact to recent highs.
- When sentiment turns positive after a dip, model often overshoots the true mean; reduce forecast by 5–10% in such cases.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model should not forecast sharp upward moves; cap upward revisions at 3–5% above recent low.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overpredict mid-term recovery after sharp declines; apply a 2–4% downward bias if sentiment is weak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overestimates price stability; adjust downward slightly to reflect mean reversion.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves after 3 consecutive days of negative sentiment; model is prone to “reversal overfitting”.
- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates the depth of the drop — add 2–5% buffer to downward forecasts.
